import warnings
warnings.filterwarnings('ignore')
from pathlib import Path

# Connect to the database
db_path = "./dacomp-072.sqlite"
if not Path(db_path).exists():

conn = sqlite3.connect(db_path)

cursor = conn.cursor()
cursor.execute("PRAGMA table_info(lever__hiring_manager_scorecard);")
columns = cursor.fetchall()
column_names = [col[1] for col in columns]

# Confidential fields
confidential_fields = ['hiring_manager_id', 'hiring_manager_name', 
                      'hiring_manager_email', 'overall_performance_score', 
                      'performance_tier']

# Safe columns for analysis
safe_columns = [col for col in column_names if col not in confidential_fields]

# Load data
if safe_columns:
    columns_str = ", ".join(safe_columns)
    query = f"SELECT {columns_str} FROM lever__hiring_manager_scorecard"
    df = pd.read_sql_query(query, conn)
    
    print(f"Analyzing {len(df)} records for outliers...")
    
    # First, let's understand what kind of data we have
    print("\n=== DATA EXPLORATION ===")
    
    # Separate categorical and numerical columns
    categorical_cols = []
    numerical_cols = []
    
    for col in df.columns:
        if df[col].dtype in ['object', 'str'] or df[col].nunique() < 10:
            categorical_cols.append(col)
        elif np.issubdtype(df[col].dtype, np.number):
            numerical_cols.append(col)
    
    print(f"Categorical columns: {categorical_cols}")
    print(f"Numerical columns: {numerical_cols}")
    
    # Show value counts for categorical columns
    for col in categorical_cols:
        print(f"\nValue distribution for '{col}':")
        value_counts = df[col].value_counts()
        for value, count in value_counts.items():
            print(f"  {value}: {count} records ({count/len(df)*100:.1f}%)")
    
    # For numerical columns, use multiple outlier detection methods
    if numerical_cols:
        print(f"\n=== OUTLIER DETECTION FOR NUMERICAL COLUMNS ===")
        
        # Prepare data for outlier detection
        X = df[numerical_cols].copy()
        
        # Handle missing values
        X_clean = X.dropna()
        if len(X_clean) < len(X):
            print(f"Note: Dropped {len(X) - len(X_clean)} records with missing values")
        
        if len(X_clean) > 0:
            # Method 1: Z-score based outliers
            print("\n1. Z-score based outlier detection (|Z| > 3):")
            z_scores = np.abs(stats.zscore(X_clean))
            outliers_z = (z_scores > 3).any(axis=1)
            
            if outliers_z.any():
                outlier_indices_z = X_clean.index[outliers_z].tolist()
                print(f"   Found {outliers_z.sum()} potential outliers using Z-score method")
                
                # Show characteristics of these outliers
                outlier_data_z = df.loc[outlier_indices_z]
                print("\n   Characteristics of Z-score outliers:")
                for idx in outlier_indices_z[:5]:  # Limit to first 5 for readability
                    print(f"\n   Record at index {idx}:")
                    for col in numerical_cols:
                        if not pd.isna(df.loc[idx, col]):
                            col_mean = X_clean[col].mean()
                            col_std = X_clean[col].std()
                            z_val = (df.loc[idx, col] - col_mean) / col_std if col_std > 0 else 0
                            if abs(z_val) > 3:
                                print(f"     {col}: {df.loc[idx, col]:.2f} (Z = {z_val:.2f}, mean = {col_mean:.2f})")
            else:
                print("   No strong outliers detected via Z-score method")
            
            # Method 2: Isolation Forest
            print("\n2. Isolation Forest outlier detection:")
            scaler = StandardScaler()
            X_scaled = scaler.fit_transform(X_clean)
            
            iso_forest = IsolationForest(contamination=0.1, random_state=42)
            outliers_iso = iso_forest.fit_predict(X_scaled)
            outlier_mask_iso = outliers_iso == -1
            
            if outlier_mask_iso.any():
                outlier_indices_iso = X_clean.index[outlier_mask_iso].tolist()
                print(f"   Found {outlier_mask_iso.sum()} potential outliers using Isolation Forest")
                
                # Show characteristics of these outliers
                print("\n   Characteristics of Isolation Forest outliers:")
                for idx in outlier_indices_iso[:5]:  # Limit to first 5
                    print(f"\n   Record at index {idx}:")
                    for col in numerical_cols:
                        if not pd.isna(df.loc[idx, col]):
                            col_mean = X_clean[col].mean()
                            col_median = X_clean[col].median()
                            if abs(df.loc[idx, col] - col_median) > 3 * X_clean[col].mad():
                                print(f"     {col}: {df.loc[idx, col]:.2f} (median = {col_median:.2f})")
            
            # Method 3: IQR-based outliers
            print("\n3. IQR-based outlier detection:")
            for col in numerical_cols:
                Q1 = X_clean[col].quantile(0.25)
                Q3 = X_clean[col].quantile(0.75)
                IQR = Q3 - Q1
                lower_bound = Q1 - 1.5 * IQR
                upper_bound = Q3 + 1.5 * IQR
                
                outliers_col = X_clean[(X_clean[col] < lower_bound) | (X_clean[col] > upper_bound)]
                if not outliers_col.empty:
                    print(f"\n   Column '{col}':")
                    print(f"     Q1: {Q1:.2f}, Q3: {Q3:.2f}, IQR: {IQR:.2f}")
                    print(f"     Bounds: [{lower_bound:.2f}, {upper_bound:.2f}]")
                    print(f"     Found {len(outliers_col)} outliers")

                        min_outlier = outliers_col[col].min()
                        max_outlier = outliers_col[col].max()
                        print(f"     Outlier range: [{min_outlier:.2f}, {max_outlier:.2f}]")
                        print(f"     vs data range: [{X_clean[col].min():.2f}, {X_clean[col].max():.2f}]")
    
    # Analyze categorical anomalies
    print(f"\n=== CATEGORICAL ANOMALIES ===")
    for col in categorical_cols:
        value_counts = df[col].value_counts()
        total = len(df[col].dropna())
        
        # Identify rare categories (less than 1% of data)
        rare_categories = []
        for value, count in value_counts.items():
            percentage = count / total * 100
            if percentage < 1.0:  # Less than 1%
                rare_categories.append((value, count, percentage))
        
        if rare_categories:
            print(f"\nColumn '{col}' has rare categories (< 1%):")
            for value, count, percentage in rare_categories:
                print(f"  '{value}': {count} records ({percentage:.2f}%)")
    
    # Cross-tabulation to find unusual combinations
    if len(categorical_cols) >= 2:
        print(f"\n=== UNUSUAL CATEGORY COMBINATIONS ===")
        # Take first two categorical columns for analysis
        col1, col2 = categorical_cols[0], categorical_cols[1]
        
        crosstab = pd.crosstab(df[col1], df[col2])
        print(f"Cross-tabulation of '{col1}' vs '{col2}':")
        
        # Find cells with very low counts
        total = crosstab.sum().sum()
        rare_combinations = []
        
        for idx in crosstab.index:
            for col in crosstab.columns:
                count = crosstab.loc[idx, col]
                if count > 0 and count / total * 100 < 0.5:  # Less than 0.5%
                    rare_combinations.append((idx, col, count))
        
        if rare_combinations:
            print(f"\nRare combinations (< 0.5% of total):")
            for val1, val2, count in rare_combinations[:10]:  # Limit to 10
                print(f"  '{val1}' & '{val2}': {count} records")
        else:
            print("No exceptionally rare combinations found")
    
    # Final summary of most anomalous records
    print(f"\n=== SUMMARY: MOST ANOMALOUS RECORDS ===")
    
    # Combine outlier detection methods
    all_outlier_indices = set()
    
    # Get Z-score outliers
    if 'X_clean' in locals() and 'outliers_z' in locals():
        if outliers_z.any():
            all_outlier_indices.update(X_clean.index[outliers_z].tolist())
    
    # Get Isolation Forest outliers
    if 'outlier_mask_iso' in locals():
        if outlier_mask_iso.any():
            all_outlier_indices.update(X_clean.index[outlier_mask_iso].tolist())
    
    if all_outlier_indices:
        print(f"Found {len(all_outlier_indices)} distinct records flagged as outliers by multiple methods")
        print("\nDetailed signatures of top 5 most anomalous records:")
        
        # Convert to list and take first 5
        outlier_list = list(all_outlier_indices)[:5]
        
        for idx in outlier_list:
            print(f"\n--- Record at index {idx} ---")
            
            # Show all column values for this record
            record = df.loc[idx]
            for col in df.columns:
                if not pd.isna(record[col]):
                    # For numerical columns, show how extreme they are
                    if col in numerical_cols and 'X_clean' in locals():
                        if col in X_clean.columns:
                            col_mean = X_clean[col].mean()
                            col_std = X_clean[col].std()
                            col_median = X_clean[col].median()
                            col_mad = X_clean[col].mad()
                            
                            if col_std > 0:
                                z_val = (record[col] - col_mean) / col_std
                                mad_ratio = abs(record[col] - col_median) / col_mad if col_mad > 0 else 0
                                
                                if abs(z_val) > 2 or mad_ratio > 3:
                                    print(f"{col}: {record[col]} (Z = {z_val:.2f}, {mad_ratio:.1f}x median deviation)")
                                else:
                                    print(f"{col}: {record[col]}")
                            else:
                                print(f"{col}: {record[col]}")
                        else:
                            print(f"{col}: {record[col]}")
                    else:
                        # For categorical, check if rare
                        if col in categorical_cols:
                            value_counts = df[col].value_counts()

                                percentage = count / len(df) * 100
                                if percentage < 5:  # Less than 5%
                                    print(f"{col}: {record[col]} (rare: {percentage:.1f}%)")
                                else:
                                    print(f"{col}: {record[col]}")
                            else:
                                print(f"{col}: {record[col]} (value not found in distribution)")
                        else:
                            print(f"{col}: {record[col]}")
    else:

    print("2. Detecting anomalies using Isolation Forest...")
    scaler = StandardScaler()

    iso_forest = IsolationForest(contamination=0.15, random_state=42)

    anomaly_scores['iso_forest_score'] = iso_scores
    
    # Method 3: Mahalanobis distance (for multivariate outliers)
    print("3. Calculating multivariate distance anomalies...")
    try:
        from scipy.spatial.distance import mahalanobis
        cov_matrix = np.cov(X_numerical_clean.T, rowvar=False)
        inv_cov_matrix = np.linalg.pinv(cov_matrix)

            try:
                dist = mahalanobis(row.values, mean_vector, inv_cov_matrix)
                mahalanobis_distances.append(dist)

    categorical_cols = []
    numerical_cols = []

        if df[col].dtype in ['object', 'str'] or df[col].nunique() < 10:
            categorical_cols.append(col)
        elif np.issubdtype(df[col].dtype, np.number):

            z_scores = np.abs(stats.zscore(X_clean))
            outliers_z = (z_scores > 3).any(axis=1)
            
            if outliers_z.any():
                outlier_indices_z = X_clean.index[outliers_z].tolist()

            # Method 2: Isolation Forest

            scaler = StandardScaler()

            iso_forest = IsolationForest(contamination=0.1, random_state=42)
            outliers_iso = iso_forest.fit_predict(X_scaled)
            outlier_mask_iso = outliers_iso == -1

                        'percentage': percentage,

                    })

        for j, feat in enumerate(anomalous_features[:5], 1):

from scipy import stats

from sklearn.preprocessing import StandardScaler
import warnings
warnings.filterwarnings('ignore')
from pathlib import Path

# Connect to the database
db_path = "./dacomp-072.sqlite"
if not Path(db_path).exists():
    print(f"Error: Database file not found at {db_path}")
    exit()

conn = sqlite3.connect(db_path)

# Get column names
cursor = conn.cursor()
cursor.execute("PRAGMA table_info(lever__hiring_manager_scorecard);")
columns = cursor.fetchall()
column_names = [col[1] for col in columns]

# Confidential fields
confidential_fields = ['hiring_manager_id', 'hiring_manager_name', 
                      'hiring_manager_email', 'overall_performance_score', 
                      'performance_tier']

# Safe columns for analysis
safe_columns = [col for col in column_names if col not in confidential_fields]

# Load data
if safe_columns:
    columns_str = ", ".join(safe_columns)
    query = f"SELECT {columns_str} FROM lever__hiring_manager_scorecard"
    df = pd.read_sql_query(query, conn)
    
    print(f"Analyzing {len(df)} records for outliers...")
    
    # First, let's understand what kind of data we have
    print("\n=== DATA EXPLORATION ===")
    
    # Separate categorical and numerical columns
    categorical_cols = []
    numerical_cols = []
    
    for col in df.columns:
        if df[col].dtype in ['object', 'str'] or df[col].nunique() < 10:
            categorical_cols.append(col)
        elif np.issubdtype(df[col].dtype, np.number):
            numerical_cols.append(col)
    
    print(f"Categorical columns: {categorical_cols}")
    print(f"Numerical columns: {numerical_cols}")
    
    # Show value counts for categorical columns
    for col in categorical_cols:
        print(f"\nValue distribution for '{col}':")
        value_counts = df[col].value_counts()
        for value, count in value_counts.items():
            print(f"  {value}: {count} records ({count/len(df)*100:.1f}%)")
    
    # For numerical columns, use multiple outlier detection methods
    if numerical_cols:
        print(f"\n=== OUTLIER DETECTION FOR NUMERICAL COLUMNS ===")
        
        # Prepare data for outlier detection
        X = df[numerical_cols].copy()
        
        # Handle missing values
        X_clean = X.dropna()
        if len(X_clean) < len(X):
            print(f"Note: Dropped {len(X) - len(X_clean)} records with missing values")
        
        if len(X_clean) > 0:
            # Method 1: Z-score based outliers
            print("\n1. Z-score based outlier detection (|Z| > 3):")
            z_scores = np.abs(stats.zscore(X_clean))
            outliers_z = (z_scores > 3).any(axis=1)
            
            if outliers_z.any():
                outlier_indices_z = X_clean.index[outliers_z].tolist()
                print(f"   Found {outliers_z.sum()} potential outliers using Z-score method")
                
                # Show characteristics of these outliers
                outlier_data_z = df.loc[outlier_indices_z]
                print("\n   Characteristics of Z-score outliers:")
                for idx in outlier_indices_z[:5]:  # Limit to first 5 for readability
                    print(f"\n   Record at index {idx}:")
                    for col in numerical_cols:
                        if not pd.isna(df.loc[idx, col]):
                            col_mean = X_clean[col].mean()
                            col_std = X_clean[col].std()
                            z_val = (df.loc[idx, col] - col_mean) / col_std if col_std > 0 else 0
                            if abs(z_val) > 3:
                                print(f"     {col}: {df.loc[idx, col]:.2f} (Z = {z_val:.2f}, mean = {col_mean:.2f})")
            else:
                print("   No strong outliers detected via Z-score method")
            
            # Method 2: Isolation Forest
            print("\n2. Isolation Forest outlier detection:")
            scaler = StandardScaler()
            X_scaled = scaler.fit_transform(X_clean)
            
            iso_forest = IsolationForest(contamination=0.1, random_state=42)
            outliers_iso = iso_forest.fit_predict(X_scaled)
            outlier_mask_iso = outliers_iso == -1
            
            if outlier_mask_iso.any():
                outlier_indices_iso = X_clean.index[outlier_mask_iso].tolist()
                print(f"   Found {outlier_mask_iso.sum()} potential outliers using Isolation Forest")
                
                # Show characteristics of these outliers
                print("\n   Characteristics of Isolation Forest outliers:")
                for idx in outlier_indices_iso[:5]:  # Limit to first 5
                    print(f"\n   Record at index {idx}:")
                    for col in numerical_cols:
                        if not pd.isna(df.loc[idx, col]):
                            col_mean = X_clean[col].mean()
                            col_median = X_clean[col].median()
                            if abs(df.loc[idx, col] - col_median) > 3 * X_clean[col].mad():
                                print(f"     {col}: {df.loc[idx, col]:.2f} (median = {col_median:.2f})")

# filename: comprehensive_outlier_analysis_fixed.py
import sqlite3
import pandas as pd
import numpy as np
from scipy import stats
from sklearn.ensemble import IsolationForest
from sklearn.preprocessing import StandardScaler
import warnings
warnings.filterwarnings('ignore')
from pathlib import Path

# Connect to the database
db_path = "./dacomp-072.sqlite"
if not Path(db_path).exists():
    print(f"Error: Database file not found at {db_path}")
    exit()

conn = sqlite3.connect(db_path)

# Get all data (excluding confidential fields)
cursor = conn.cursor()
cursor.execute("PRAGMA table_info(lever__hiring_manager_scorecard);")
columns = cursor.fetchall()
all_column_names = [col[1] for col in columns]

# Confidential fields - cannot appear in row-level outputs
confidential_fields = ['hiring_manager_id', 'hiring_manager_name', 
                      'hiring_manager_email', 'overall_performance_score', 
                      'performance_tier']

# Safe columns for analysis
safe_columns = [col for col in all_column_names if col not in confidential_fields]

# Load the data
columns_str = ", ".join(safe_columns)
query = f"SELECT {columns_str} FROM lever__hiring_manager_scorecard"
df = pd.read_sql_query(query, conn)

print("=== DATA SUMMARY ===")
print(f"Total records: {len(df)}")
print(f"Columns for analysis: {len(safe_columns)}")

# Identify data types
categorical_cols = []
numerical_cols = []

for col in df.columns:
    if df[col].dtype == 'object' or df[col].nunique() < 10:
        categorical_cols.append(col)
    elif np.issubdtype(df[col].dtype, np.number):
        numerical_cols.append(col)

print(f"\nNumerical columns ({len(numerical_cols)}): {numerical_cols}")
print(f"Categorical columns ({len(categorical_cols)}): {categorical_cols}")

# Create an anomaly score for each record using multiple methods
print("\n=== COMPREHENSIVE ANOMALY DETECTION ===")

# Prepare numerical data for analysis
X_numerical = df[numerical_cols].copy()
X_numerical_clean = X_numerical.dropna()

if len(X_numerical_clean) > 0:
    # Method 1: Z-score anomalies
    print("\n1. Detecting statistical outliers using Z-scores...")
    z_scores = np.abs(stats.zscore(X_numerical_clean, nan_policy='omit'))
    
    # Create anomaly scores
    anomaly_scores = pd.DataFrame(index=df.index)
    anomaly_scores['z_score_max'] = np.nanmax(z_scores, axis=1) if z_scores.size > 0 else 0
    
    # Method 2: Isolation Forest
    print("2. Detecting anomalies using Isolation Forest...")
    scaler = StandardScaler()
    X_scaled = scaler.fit_transform(X_numerical_clean.fillna(X_numerical_clean.median()))
    
    iso_forest = IsolationForest(contamination=0.15, random_state=42)
    iso_scores = iso_forest.fit_predict(X_scaled)
    anomaly_scores['iso_forest_score'] = iso_scores
    
    # Method 3: Mahalanobis distance (for multivariate outliers)
    print("3. Calculating multivariate distance anomalies...")
    try:
        from scipy.spatial.distance import mahalanobis
        cov_matrix = np.cov(X_numerical_clean.T, rowvar=False)
        inv_cov_matrix = np.linalg.pinv(cov_matrix)
        mean_vector = X_numerical_clean.mean(axis=0).values
        
        mahalanobis_distances = []
        for i, row in X_numerical_clean.iterrows():
            try:
                dist = mahalanobis(row.values, mean_vector, inv_cov_matrix)
                mahalanobis_distances.append(dist)
            except:
                mahalanobis_distances.append(np.nan)
        
        anomaly_scores['mahalanobis_dist'] = mahalanobis_distances
    except Exception as e:
        print(f"   Note: Mahalanobis distance calculation skipped: {e}")
        anomaly_scores['mahalanobis_dist'] = 0
    
    # Combine scores
    anomaly_scores['combined_score'] = (
        anomaly_scores['z_score_max'].fillna(0) * 0.4 +
        (anomaly_scores['iso_forest_score'] == -1).astype(int) * 0.4 +
        anomaly_scores['mahalanobis_dist'].fillna(0) / anomaly_scores['mahalanobis_dist'].fillna(1).max() * 0.2
    )
    
    # Identify top outliers
    top_outlier_count = min(10, len(df) // 10)  # Top ~10% as outliers
    outlier_indices = anomaly_scores.nlargest(top_outlier_count, 'combined_score').index
    
    print(f"\nIdentified {len(outlier_indices)} most anomalous records")
    
    # Analyze categorical anomalies for these outliers
    print("\n=== DETAILED ANOMALY PROFILES ===")
    
    for i, idx in enumerate(outlier_indices, 1):
        record = df.loc[idx]
        
        print(f"\n{'='*60}")
        print(f"ANOMALY #{i} (Index: {idx})")
        print(f"Overall anomaly score: {anomaly_scores.loc[idx, 'combined_score']:.3f}")
        
        # Check which features make this record anomalous
        anomalous_features = []
        
        # Numerical anomalies
        for col in numerical_cols:
            if col in X_numerical_clean.columns:
                value = record[col]
                if not pd.isna(value):
                    col_mean = X_numerical_clean[col].mean()
                    col_std = X_numerical_clean[col].std()
                    col_median = X_numerical_clean[col].median()
                    
                    if col_std > 0:
                        z_score = abs((value - col_mean) / col_std)
                        median_deviation = abs(value - col_median) / (X_numerical_clean[col].quantile(0.75) - X_numerical_clean[col].quantile(0.25))
                        
                        if z_score > 2.5 or median_deviation > 3:
                            percentile = stats.percentileofscore(X_numerical_clean[col].dropna(), value)
                            direction = "above" if value > col_median else "below"
                            
                            anomalous_features.append({
                                'feature': col,
                                'value': value,
                                'z_score': z_score,
                                'percentile': percentile,
                                'direction': direction,
                                'population_median': col_median
                            })
        
        # Categorical anomalies
        for col in categorical_cols:
            value = record[col]
            if pd.isna(value):
                continue
                
            value_counts = df[col].value_counts()
            if value in value_counts.index:
                frequency = value_counts[value]
                percentage = frequency / len(df) * 100
                
                if percentage < 5:  # Rare category (< 5%)
                    anomalous_features.append({
                        'feature': col,
                        'value': value,
                        'frequency': frequency,
                        'percentage': percentage,
                        'type': 'rare_category'
                    })
        
        # Sort features by how anomalous they are
        anomalous_features.sort(key=lambda x: x.get('z_score', 0) if 'z_score' in x else 100 - x.get('percentage', 0), reverse=True)
        
        # Display top anomalous features
        print(f"\nKey anomalous attributes (top 5):")
        for j, feat in enumerate(anomalous_features[:5], 1):
            if 'z_score' in feat:
                print(f"  {j}. {feat['feature']}: {feat['value']:.2f} ")
                print(f"     (Z-score: {feat['z_score']:.2f}, {feat['direction']} {abs(feat['value'] - feat['population_median']):.2f} from median, {feat['percentile']:.1f}th percentile)")
            else:
                print(f"  {j}. {feat['feature']}: '{feat['value']}'")
                print(f"     (Rare: only {feat['frequency']} occurrences, {feat['percentage']:.1f}% of population)")
        
        # Show cross-feature patterns
        print(f"\nNotable cross-feature patterns:")
        
        # Check for unusual combinations
        if 'decision_speed_category' in df.columns and 'avg_total_days_to_hire' in df.columns:
            ds_category = record['decision_speed_category']
            days_to_hire = record['avg_total_days_to_hire']
            
            # Get typical ranges for this decision speed category
            category_data = df[df['decision_speed_category'] == ds_category]
            if len(category_data) > 0:
                typical_days = category_data['avg_total_days_to_hire'].median()
                if abs(days_to_hire - typical_days) > typical_days * 0.5:  # 50% different from typical
                    print(f"  • Decision speed '{ds_category}' with {days_to_hire:.1f} days to hire")
                    print(f"    (vs typical {typical_days:.1f} days for this category)")
        
        if 'hiring_specialization' in df.columns and 'total_candidates_hired' in df.columns:
            specialization = record['hiring_specialization']
            candidates_hired = record['total_candidates_hired']
            
            specialization_data = df[df['hiring_specialization'] == specialization]
            if len(specialization_data) > 0:
                typical_hired = specialization_data['total_candidates_hired'].median()
                if abs(candidates_hired - typical_hired) > typical_hired * 0.6:  # 60% different
                    print(f"  • {specialization} with {candidates_hired} candidates hired")
                    print(f"    (vs typical {typical_hired:.0f} for this specialization)")
    
    # Now let's analyze outliers by aggregation groups (respecting policy)
    print(f"\n{'='*60}")
    print("=== AGGREGATED ANALYSIS (Policy Compliant) ===")
    print("Analyzing outliers at allowed aggregation levels...")
    
    # Aggregation by performance_tier (though we can't show individual performance_tier values)
    # Instead, we'll aggregate by allowed dimensions
    aggregation_dimensions = ['decision_speed_category', 'hiring_specialization']
    
    for dim in aggregation_dimensions:
        if dim in df.columns:
            print(f"\nOutlier analysis by {dim}:")
            
            # Calculate statistics for each group
            group_stats = df.groupby(dim).agg({
                'total_candidates_hired': ['count', 'mean', 'std', 'min', 'max'],
                'avg_total_days_to_hire': ['mean', 'std', 'min', 'max'],
                'requisition_fill_rate': ['mean', 'std', 'min', 'max']
            }).round(2)
            
            print(f"Group statistics for {dim}:")
            for group_name in group_stats.index:
                group_data = df[df[dim] == group_name]
                
                # Find records in this group that are outliers within the group
                if len(group_data) > 3:  # Need enough data
                    # Calculate Z-scores within group for key metrics
                    for metric in ['total_candidates_hired', 'avg_total_days_to_hire', 'requisition_fill_rate']:
                        if metric in df.columns:
                            group_values = group_data[metric].dropna()
                            if len(group_values) > 2 and group_values.std() > 0:
                                group_z_scores = np.abs((group_values - group_values.mean()) / group_values.std())
                                extreme_records = group_z_scores[group_z_scores > 2.5]
                                
                                if len(extreme_records) > 0:
                                    print(f"  • {group_name}: {len(extreme_records)} extreme {metric} values")
                                    # Can't show individual records, but can describe patterns
                                    extreme_indices = extreme_records.index.tolist()
                                    if extreme_indices:
                                        # Get the actual extreme values (aggregated description)
                                        min_val = group_data.loc[extreme_indices, metric].min()
                                        max_val = group_data.loc[extreme_indices, metric].max()
                                        print(f"    Range: {min_val:.1f} to {max_val:.1f} (group mean: {group_values.mean():.1f})")
            
            # Identify groups that are themselves anomalous
            print(f"\nAnomalous {dim} groups (vs overall population):")
            
            for metric in ['total_candidates_hired', 'avg_total_days_to_hire']:
                if metric in df.columns:
                    overall_mean = df[metric].mean()
                    overall_std = df[metric].std()
                    
                    for group_name in group_stats.index:
                        group_mean = df[df[dim] == group_name][metric].mean()
                        if overall_std > 0:
                            group_z = abs((group_mean - overall_mean) / overall_std)
                            if group_z > 1.5:  # Group is significantly different
                                direction = "above" if group_mean > overall_mean else "below"
                                print(f"  • {group_name}: {metric} {direction} average")
                                print(f"    (Group: {group_mean:.1f}, Overall: {overall_mean:.1f}, Z: {group_z:.2f})")
    
    # Final summary of anomaly types
    print(f"\n{'='*60}")
    print("=== ANOMALY TYPES SUMMARY ===")
    
    # Classify anomalies by type
    anomaly_types = {
        'extreme_volume': [],
        'extreme_timing': [],
        'extreme_efficiency': [],
        'rare_combinations': []
    }
    
    for idx in outlier_indices:
        record = df.loc[idx]
        
        # Check for extreme volume
        volume_metrics = ['total_candidates_hired', 'total_applications_received', 'total_interviews_coordinated']
        volume_z_scores = []
        for metric in volume_metrics:
            if metric in numerical_cols and metric in X_numerical_clean.columns:
                value = record[metric]
                if not pd.isna(value):
                    z = abs((value - X_numerical_clean[metric].mean()) / X_numerical_clean[metric].std())
                    volume_z_scores.append(z)
        
        if volume_z_scores and max(volume_z_scores) > 2.5:
            anomaly_types['extreme_volume'].append(idx)
        
        # Check for extreme timing
        timing_metrics = ['avg_total_days_to_hire', 'avg_candidate_lifecycle_days']
        timing_z_scores = []
        for metric in timing_metrics:
            if metric in numerical_cols and metric in X_numerical_clean.columns:
                value = record[metric]
                if not pd.isna(value):
                    z = abs((value - X_numerical_clean[metric].mean()) / X_numerical_clean[metric].std())
                    timing_z_scores.append(z)
        
        if timing_z_scores and max(timing_z_scores) > 2.5:
            anomaly_types['extreme_timing'].append(idx)
        
        # Check for extreme efficiency
        efficiency_metrics = ['requisition_fill_rate', 'candidate_hire_rate', 'interview_success_rate']
        efficiency_z_scores = []
        for metric in efficiency_metrics:
            if metric in numerical_cols and metric in X_numerical_clean.columns:
                value = record[metric]
                if not pd.isna(value):
                    z = abs((value - X_numerical_clean[metric].mean()) / X_numerical_clean[metric].std())
                    efficiency_z_scores.append(z)
        
        if efficiency_z_scores and max(efficiency_z_scores) > 2.5:
            anomaly_types['extreme_efficiency'].append(idx)
    
    print(f"Anomaly classification for {len(outlier_indices)} outliers:")
    for anomaly_type, indices in anomaly_types.items():
        if indices:
            type_name = anomaly_type.replace('_', ' ').title()
            print(f"  • {type_name}: {len(indices)} records")
            
            # Show one example characteristic
            if indices:
                example_idx = indices[0]
                example_record = df.loc[example_idx]
                
                if anomaly_type == 'extreme_volume':
                    example_metric = 'total_candidates_hired'
                    if example_metric in df.columns:
                        value = example_record[example_metric]
                        mean = df[example_metric].mean()
                        print(f"    Example: {value:.0f} candidates hired (vs average {mean:.0f})")
                
                elif anomaly_type == 'extreme_timing':
                    example_metric = 'avg_total_days_to_hire'
                    if example_metric in df.columns:
                        value = example_record[example_metric]
                        mean = df[example_metric].mean()
                        print(f"    Example: {value:.1f} days to hire (vs average {mean:.1f})")
                
                elif anomaly_type == 'extreme_efficiency':
                    example_metric = 'requisition_fill_rate'
                    if example_metric in df.columns:
                        value = example_record[example_metric]
                        mean = df[example_metric].mean()
                        print(f"    Example: {value:.3f} fill rate (vs average {mean:.3f})")

else:
    print("Insufficient numerical data for anomaly detection")
